intro: Hands-on A+ Core 2 labs graded in your browser: a Windows command-line malware cleanup, Linux permissions and services, mapped drives, workstation hardening in a settings console, and malware, backup and change-management drills. Simulated, so some details are simplified.

labs.title: Clean up a compromised workstation
labs.summary: Use tasklist, taskkill, schtasks and net commands to stop a malicious process, remove its persistence and an unauthorized admin account, then repair system files.
labs.scenario: Antivirus flagged updater_svc.exe on WS-114. You're in an elevated command prompt. Investigation notes: the malware reinstalls itself with a scheduled task named SysHelperUpdate, and someone added a local account helpdesk_tmp to Administrators. Clean it up without reimaging (the user has already been disconnected from the network).

tasks.text: Remove helpdesk_tmp from Administrators and disable the account

hints: net localgroup administrators helpdesk_tmp /delete then net user helpdesk_tmp /active:no.
labs.solution:
tasklist
taskkill /im updater_svc.exe /f
schtasks /query
schtasks /delete /tn SysHelperUpdate /f
net localgroup administrators
net localgroup administrators helpdesk_tmp /delete
net user helpdesk_tmp /active:no
sfc /scannow
gpupdate /force
labs.review: Removing malware means stopping it, removing its persistence (tasks, services, run keys), reversing privilege changes, and repairing the OS. Then follow the full CompTIA removal steps.

labs.title: Linux file permissions and services
labs.summary: Navigate a Linux server, fix file permissions and ownership, install a package with apt, and start and enable a service.
labs.scenario:
You're student on web01 (Ubuntu) with sudo rights. Tasks from the team lead:

  • Make ~/scripts/backup.sh executable by you (and readable by others, not writable)
  • Give the student account ownership of /srv/reports/q3.csv
  • Create a ~/archive directory
  • Install the nginx package, then make sure the nginx service is running and starts at boot

tasks.text: nginx is running and enabled at boot

hints: Changing an owner needs root: sudo chown student /srv/reports/q3.csv.
sudo apt install nginx, then sudo systemctl enable --now nginx.
labs.solution:
ls -l scripts
chmod 755 scripts/backup.sh
sudo chown student /srv/reports/q3.csv
mkdir ~/archive
sudo apt update
sudo apt install nginx
sudo systemctl enable --now nginx
systemctl status nginx
labs.review: Octal permissions are owner/group/other with r=4, w=2, x=1. Ownership changes and package installs need sudo; systemctl enable makes a service start at boot, while start runs it now.

labs.title: Malware types and the removal process
labs.summary: Identify malware types from their behavior and order CompTIA's best-practice malware removal steps.
labs.scenario: You're writing the help desk's malware runbook.

activities.title: Malware types
activities.prompt: Match each behavior to the malware type.

items.text: Pretends to be useful software but carries a malicious payload
Hides deep in the OS to conceal itself and other malware
Uses the CPU/GPU to generate cryptocurrency
Secretly monitors browsing and collects data

activities.title: Malware removal steps
activities.prompt: Arrange the best-practice malware removal steps in order.
items: Enable System Restore and create a restore point (Windows Home)

hints: System Restore is disabled before cleaning so infected restore points are removed, then re-enabled afterward.
labs.review: The order matters: confirm, isolate, clean without reinfecting from restore points, protect, and make sure the user knows how it happened.

labs.title: Harden a Windows workstation
labs.summary: Use a workstation settings console to enable encryption, firewall and updates, tighten accounts and screen locking, and disable risky features.
labs.scenario: A new laptop for the finance team must meet the security baseline: full-disk encryption, all firewall profiles on, automatic updates, real-time antivirus, the Guest account disabled, a 5-minute screen lock, UAC at its default or higher, AutoRun off and Remote Desktop off. Save each page.

fields.label: User Account Control
options: Notify only when apps make changes (no dim)
Notify only when apps make changes (default)

tasks.text: All three firewall profiles on and real-time antivirus on
Guest disabled and a 5-minute screen lock
UAC at the default level or higher

in: Notify only when apps make changes (default)

hints: The public firewall profile protects the laptop on coffee-shop and hotel networks.
labs.solution: Accounts: Guest off, 5 minutes, default UAC. Security: everything on. System: Automatic updates, AutoRun off, Remote Desktop off.
labs.review: These settings come straight from the Core 2 workstation security objectives: encryption, firewall, AV, patching, account and login hardening, and disabling AutoRun.

labs.title: Backups and operational procedures
labs.summary: Match backup types to how they work, apply the 3-2-1 rule, and identify what belongs in a change request.
labs.scenario: You're documenting backup and change procedures for a small business.

activities.title: Backup types
activities.prompt: Match each description to its backup type.

items.text: Copies changes since the last backup of any kind
Copies changes since the last full backup
Builds a new full backup from the last full plus later incrementals

activities.title: Change management
activities.prompt: Which items belong in a change request form, and which are separate steps?

items.text: Purpose and scope of the change

hints: Restoring incrementals needs the full plus every incremental; restoring a differential needs the full plus the latest differential.
labs.review: Backup type affects backup time and restore time in opposite ways. Change requests document purpose, scope, risk and affected systems before approval.

labs.title: Map network drives from the command line
labs.summary: Inspect, remove and create mapped network drives with net use, and check a user's group membership.
labs.scenario: A user in Finance can't open shared spreadsheets. Their Y: drive points to a decommissioned server. Map Z: to \\FS01\Finance and remove the stale mapping. Also confirm the user mchen is in the Finance group.

tasks.text: Check mchen's groups with net user mchen

labs.solution:
net use
net use Y: /delete
net use Z: \\FS01\Finance
net user mchen
labs.review: net use maps and removes drive letters for SMB shares; net user shows account details including group memberships.

labs.title: Troubleshoot: 'The printer won't print'
labs.summary: Use a print-server console to find why an HR printer stopped printing: a stale port address, a stuck job and 'use printer offline' left on.
labs.scenario:
HR says the HR-HP-M404 printer stopped printing this morning; the print queue shows a job that never finishes. The printer's display says it is online with IP 192.168.1.61. Last week the office switched its DHCP range, and printers without reservations may have received new addresses.

Work through the console: look at the printer, the queue and the port, fix what is wrong, then Save changes on each page. Don't delete printers or other people's jobs.

fields.label: Use printer offline
fields.help: When on, jobs are held instead of sent to the printer.

fields.label: Port (printer address)
fields.help: The IP address the server sends jobs to.

tasks.text: Point the printer's port at its real address, 192.168.1.61
Turn off Use printer offline and set the status to Ready
Clear only the stuck job (Offer letter.docx); the other jobs stay
Keep the other two jobs in the queue
Leave the spooler running and the driver unchanged

questions.prompt: What most likely stopped the printing?
options: The printer got a new IP address but the server's port still points at the old one
The users lack permission to print

hints: Compare the printer's display address with the port configured on the server.
A stuck job in 'Error - printing' blocks the queue behind it.
Delete a row with its Remove button, then Save.
labs.solution: Printer page: port 192.168.1.61, Use printer offline off, status Ready. Queue page: remove the errored job. Save each page.
labs.review: Classic ladder for printing problems: is the printer reachable (right address), is the queue healthy (stuck job), is the spooler running, and only then drivers and permissions. Static or reserved addresses for printers prevent this one.
